Part 01 · Content & community

How I’d contribute through content & community

Two YouTube formats and one community format, each built to be repeatable and easy to repurpose across channels.

01YouTubeFounder-led storytelling

I’d build “Inside Runable”

A recurring vlog series that makes the journey of building Runable worth following.

I’d work with the founder and team to turn the real experience of building an AI startup into a compelling content series: everyday office life, product launches, team conversations, ambitious goals, unexpected challenges, and the decisions behind the product.

Episodes I’d love to create
  • A Day Inside an AI Startup Building the Future of Work
  • What Building an AI Startup Actually Looks Like
  • Inside Runable: What We’re Building This Week
  • The Real Story Behind Our Latest Launch

How I’d execute it

Develop the episode concepts and hooks, coordinate filming with the team, shape the narrative and edits, and repurpose each vlog into Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and founder-led posts.

What this could build

A recognizable company story that helps audiences connect with the people behind Runable, not just the product.

02YouTubeInterview format

I’d create “The Runable Take”

Conversations with interesting people about how they think, work, and build.

Inspired by Career Ladder’s career-focused interview format, I’d explore a Runable series with a distinctive recurring concept, signature questions, and a visual identity people can recognize instantly. Rather than conventional sit-down interviews, each episode would revolve around a memorable question or interaction connected to work, productivity, and automation.

Episode ideas
  • We Asked Founders What They’d Automate First
  • What’s One Task You’d Never Want to Do Manually Again?
  • Show Us the Workflow That Runs Your Day
  • One Problem. One Workflow. One Better Way to Work.

How I’d execute it

Identify guests, develop the interview format, create distinctive hooks and episode titles, coordinate production, and distribute the full interviews alongside short clips across social channels.

What this could build

A repeatable content property that gives Runable a recognizable voice and attracts audiences through interesting people and conversations.

03CommunityProduct discovery

I’d launch “Let the Internet Challenge Runable”

Turn audience participation into a recurring source of content and product discovery.

I’d build a format where people submit the most tedious, ridiculous, or time-consuming tasks they wish they could automate. Runable picks a challenge, attempts to solve it using its product, and shares the process and actual outcome.

How I’d bring it to life
  • Collect submissions through Instagram Stories, comments, and creator communities.
  • Select interesting challenges that demonstrate Runable’s capabilities.
  • Produce engaging demonstrations showing the workflow and result.
  • Credit contributors and invite the audience to submit the next challenge.

What this could build

A feedback loop where the community inspires content, content demonstrates product utility, and the best use cases give new users a reason to try Runable.

Part 02 · Reach

How I’d expand Runable’s reach

More credible voices online, and a campaign that brings the product promise into the real world.

04LinkedInEmployee-led distribution

I’d turn every team member into a storyteller

A personalized LinkedIn content system that helps each team member share their own perspective.

Instead of relying only on the company page or identical reposts, each person at Runable gets ideas and drafts that fit their role and voice.

What I’d set up
  • Personalized post ideas based on each person’s role, interests, and expertise.
  • Content around product development, design decisions, lessons from building, customer problems, and life at Runable.
  • A weekly content calendar with suggested hooks, drafts, and relevant company updates.
  • A simple workflow for reviewing, personalizing, and publishing posts in each person’s authentic voice.

How I’d measure it

Employee participation, relevant audience reach, engagement, profile visits, referral traffic, and product sign-ups where attributable.

What this could build

A wider network of credible voices introducing Runable to professional audiences, including people who may later become users, advocates, or collaborators.

05Instagram + OfflineCreative direction

I’d make Runable more recognizable, on and offline

More distinctive visual storytelling, plus an unconventional campaign that brings the product promise into the real world.

One concept: The Museum of Manual Work. Imagine a pop-up installation or a series of oversized street posters celebrating the absurd tasks we still do by hand: copying data between spreadsheets, chasing updates, and repeating the same workflow for the hundredth time. Each exhibit could lead through a QR code to a relevant Runable demonstration.

The exhibits
  • Copying data between spreadsheets
  • Chasing updates
  • Repeating the same workflow for the hundredth time

How I’d execute it

Develop the creative concept, visual direction, messaging, activation ideas, and social content around the campaign. I’d first assess feasibility, audience fit, and budget before recommending a rollout.

What this could build

A memorable brand experience that generates shareable content and connects offline attention to product discovery.

Part 03 · My first 30 days at Runable

From ideas to execution

I’d start with a focused set of experiments, learn from the audience, and build on the formats that show the most promise.

01Week

Research & plan

Understand the product, audience, current content, and founder’s vision. Finalize the vlog and interview concepts, creative direction, and distribution plan.

02Week

Create & launch

Develop the first vlog or interview pilot, prepare short-form content, and establish personalized LinkedIn content frameworks for the team.

03Week

Distribute & experiment

Publish across YouTube and Instagram, initiate creator and community participation, and develop the offline activation concept.

04Week

Measure & refine

Review watch time, shares, audience engagement, employee participation, and attributable product sign-ups where measurable. Use the findings to prioritize the next cycle.
